__doc__: Tag-site scoring config. Score = weighted sum of the criteria below; each
criterion adds `weight` points to a residue when its test passes (missing
data = 0 points, never a penalty).
TO EDIT AN EXISTING SCORE: change its `weight` (0 disables it), `label`
(shown when a residue fails it), or the values in `params` (e.g. thresholds).
This is the ONLY file you touch for that.
TO ADD A NEW SCORE: add a criterion object below. If it uses one of the
existing `type` handlers (range_absent | range_present | column_below |
reagent_min_below | reagent_min_above | flank_small_fraction) you edit ONLY this
file. A brand-new kind of test needs one new handler function in
utils/scoring.py (SCORE_HANDLERS).
Criterion keys starting with "user_" are reserved for mask criteria the app/CLI
synthesizes at runtime from user choices (isoform/topology restrictions — see
utils/tag_filters.py, utils.scoring.position_mask_criterion/build_user_criteria);
don't use that prefix for a criterion authored here. Their handler type,
"position_masked", isn't meant to be authored in this file either — it takes an
explicit runtime position set, not a params dict computable from this config alone.
MASKING (issue #38): a criterion with "mask": true (and weight 0) is a
categorical disqualifier rather than a scored test — if it fires, the residue's
score is forced to 0 regardless of every other criterion, it's never suggested,
and the Results tab shows it in a distinct color with the mask label as the
tooltip. Missing data never masks (same rule as scored criteria).
Handler params reference:
range_absent:          sources (list), exclude_descriptions (list, optional),
include_descriptions (list, optional)
range_present:         sources (list), exclude_descriptions (list, optional),
include_descriptions (list, optional)
column_below:          analysis (aa_df column type, e.g. 'plddt'/'blast'), threshold
column_ramp:           analysis, low, high — the graded form of column_below. A value at
or past `low` earns the full weight, one at or past `high` earns
none, and it is linear between; `low` is always the good end, so
low > high for a track where a higher value is better. Missing
data still scores 0 and never penalizes.
reagent_min_below:     column (reagents TSV column), threshold
reagent_min_above:     columns (list of reagents TSV columns), threshold
flank_small_fraction:  small_aa (string of residue letters), window, fraction
include_descriptions/exclude_descriptions match as a case-insensitive substring
of the range's description (descriptions are often composite, e.g.
'Transmembrane: Helical (PubMed:123)').
How scored residues become suggested sites.
The top of a protein's score is a plateau, not a peak: most top-scoring residues sit
where the conservation ramp is clipped, so the score genuinely cannot rank them. Residues
tied at the best score with an identical set of satisfied BIOLOGICAL criteria therefore
form one region — equivalent places to tag. Masks and any change of biological criteria
split a region.
One site is offered per region, widest region first, up to `max_sites`. The count is
data-driven: a protein with two regions offers two, never padded to the cap with
lower-scoring residues.
The residue chosen WITHIN a region is a purely technical call, since every residue there
scores the same biologically:
pick = weight_proximity * prox + weight_margin * margin
prox    ramped on cut-to-insert distance: full credit at or below cut_near_bp, none at
or above cut_far_bp. Flat below cut_near_bp so the pick does not thrash on
differences with no experimental consequence.
margin  depth into the region, 1 at its centre and 0 at either edge (self-normalizing,
so it still discriminates in the narrow regions that are the majority).
RS3 is deliberately NOT a term here. A weight sweep over 300 worm proteins moved the cut
distance not at all (median 3.0 bp and 73.1% within 5 bp at weights 0.0, 0.3 and 0.6) and
the chosen guide's RS3 median only 0.657 -> 0.671 -> 0.689. The term bought almost nothing
while costing the project its single clean rule that scoring never influences guide choice.
`technical_criteria` are the criteria describing reagent availability rather than biology.
They are excluded when deciding whether two residues are equivalent, so a guide appearing
or disappearing never splits a region. List any new reagent-availability criterion here.
`min_spacing` keeps the offers in distinct places. Two regions can be adjacent when the
criteria they satisfy differ (equal score, different reasons), and offering both spends
the cap on what reads as one location: vab-1 otherwise returns 540/545 and 1018/1022 as
four of its five sites. A region dropped this way is replaced by the next one that does
clear the gap, so the cap still fills when the protein has somewhere else to offer.
Whether each terminus is safe to tag. Judged separately from the per-residue score,
which was built for internal sites: the features predicting C-terminal failure and
internal mislocalization are uncorrelated (rho 0.028 over 35 features), and the motifs
that matter at a terminus (PTS1, H/KDEL, KKXX, CAAX) are properties of the protein
rather than of a residue.
Three tiers, each carrying human-readable reasons:
masked    a curated annotation says the terminus is functional, or the position is
already masked by a scoring criterion (transmembrane, signal peptide, ...)
putative  a regex motif fired with no curated annotation to back it, or a track_rule
fired. Suspicion, not certainty: measured against UniProt's own terminal
annotations in yeast, H/KDEL is 100% precise but CAAX is 38.6%, PTS1 20.0%
and RAB prenylation 9.1%, so a motif hit cannot carry a curated call's weight
ok        nothing found
A flagged terminus is never withheld. Its Add button is styled as a warning and the
first click explains why and adds nothing; a second click adds the site anyway.
window                       residues from the end that count as 'at the terminus'.
curated_sources              annotation sources treated as curated evidence.
curated_blocking             case-insensitive substrings of a feature's description that
make the terminus tier 1 (same matching convention as the
criteria handlers' include_descriptions). These are point
or short features whose window overlap really does put the
terminus inside them. Span topology (transmembrane, signal
and transit peptide) is deliberately NOT listed: a window
overlap there only means the end is NEAR a helix, which is
the normal shape of a membrane protein's cytosolic tail
(unc-47's last TM ends at 477 of 486, so the tail was being
masked by proximity). A terminus actually inside one is
still tier 1 through the in_membrane_or_cleaved mask at the
terminal residue itself, which reads three predictors.
curated_requires_experimental  when true, only descriptions citing a PubMed ID count as
curated and '(predicted)' ones fall to putative. Leave false:
97% of worm terminal blocking annotations are predicted
(152 of 156) against 73% in yeast, so enabling it empties the
masked tier for worm. Meaningful only where curation is dense.
curated_mask_keys            which scoring mask criteria confer the masked tier, as
fnmatch patterns over the criterion key. A mask is only as
good as its evidence: in_membrane_or_cleaved rests on
several agreeing predictors and is corroborated by curated
annotation 86.4% of the time in worm and 85.5% in yeast,
while in_highconf_modification rests on a regex alone and
manages 4.9% / 18.9%. Masks outside this list still mask the
residue for scoring; they only drop the terminus to putative.
user_* keeps the runtime user restrictions (no N-term, no
C-term, isoform and topology filters) at the masked tier,
since those are explicit instructions rather than evidence.
putative_sources             sources whose ranges raise the putative tier (the regex
motifs from tables/modification_sites.txt).
track_rules                  extra putative rules over the per-residue tracks. A rule
aggregates one track (named by analysis type, since task
names vary per run) over `window` residues at the terminus
with `agg`, then tests either a bound (above / below) or,
with above_other_end_by, the same window at the OTHER end.
Each `requires` entry is a further gate on another track.
The two shipped rules both rest on conservation, the only
continuous signal that replicates. Absolute: JSD mean over
the terminal 10 gives 2.3x enrichment for C-terminal
construction failure in essential yeast genes at 46% recall
(N-terminal w20: 2.8x, 28%). Relative: the more conserved of
the two ends is the worse end to tag, AUROC 0.698 against
the Gameiro competition alpha (essential, signal peptides
removed; 0.637 over all ORFs). The relative rule's margin is
0.30 because the honest baseline is harsh: among confident
calls the N end is the loser 69.2% of the time, so always
guessing N is already 69.2% accurate. Flagging the more
conserved end beats that only at a wide margin - 63.9% at
of worm N termini and 4.6% of C termini. It is a weak rule
and is set to flag rarely. pLDDT appears only as a gate,
suppressing a conservation call on a floppy, badly modelled
tail; it carries no signal of its own. rSASA is deliberately
absent: terminal residues are almost all fully exposed
(median 1.03-1.14, none below 0.25), it is collinear with
pLDDT at rho -0.69, and it discriminates nothing at any
window or label even among confidently modelled termini.
The thresholds are quantile-chosen on yeast, not fitted, and
the best window differs by dataset (5 vs 10-20) on shallow
curves, so treat them as starting values to re-tune.
warn_tiers                   which tiers make the Add button warn and require a second
click. ["masked"] by default; use ["masked", "putative"] to
warn on everything that is not OK to tag.
arm_timeout_s                how long the confirm stays armed after the first click.

track_rules.label: more conserved than the other terminus

criteria.label: not in domain
criteria.note: 1 pt if residue is outside all Pfam/Phobius/DeepTMHMM domains

criteria.label: not in modification
criteria.note: 1 pt if not inside a known PTM/modification site

criteria.label: not in hydrophobic patch
criteria.note: 1 pt if not inside a hydrophobic surface patch

criteria.label: not in UniProt feature
criteria.note: 1 pt if residue is outside a blocking UniProt feature (lipidation, propeptide, signal peptide, etc.)

criteria.label: pLDDT>0.7
criteria.note: 1 pt if AlphaFold pLDDT is below threshold (disordered/flexible). 0.7 is AlphaFold's own low/confident band edge: yeast essential C-terminal failure is 7.9% below 50 and 7.6% from 50-70, then 16.1% from 70-90 and 15.3% above 90 — one break at 70, not a gradient. The former 0.5 split very-low from low, where nothing differs (a10)

criteria.label: conservation
criteria.note: graded: full point at SJD <= 0.635, none at >= 0.831, linear between. Failure rate climbs steadily across that range with no plateau, so the former hard cut at 0.5 sat below where anything happens and scored 0.51 the same as 0.95. Worth ~3x the fixed step on held-out log loss (a10)

criteria.label: guide<10bp
criteria.note: DISABLED (weight 0, kept so the database's criterion bitmask keeps its positions). Guide proximity is reagent availability, not protein biology: it had the largest spread of any criterion, and dropping it improved the independent Gameiro fitness correlation (rho 0.058 -> 0.067) while barely moving the worm choices

criteria.label: not near splice site
criteria.note: 1 pt if the nearest splice site is at least `threshold` bp away

criteria.label: few small flanking
criteria.note: 1 pt if >`fraction` of the +/-`window` flank are small AAs

criteria.label: transmembrane / signal / propeptide
criteria.note: masks the residue outright: never a good tag site (issue #38)

criteria.label: high-confidence modification
criteria.note: masks the residue outright: lipidation/prenylation sites, not soft PDZ/degron motifs (issue #38)
